title: On the Criteria To Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules
locator: pp.1054-1057; The Criteria; Efficiency and Implementation
claim: Compares processing-step decomposition with hiding design decisions; explicitly discusses implementation overhead.
limitations: Illustrative argument, not broad comparative experiment.

title: End-to-End Arguments in System Design
locator: PDF pp.2-6; duplicate suppression; performance tradeoffs
claim: Application knowledge can be necessary for correctness even when lower layers provide related mechanisms.
limitations: Not a blanket prohibition on lower-layer reliability.

title: Brewer's Conjecture and the Feasibility of Consistent, Available, Partition-Tolerant Web Services
claim: Proves impossibility under defined asynchronous assumptions; consistency means linearizability, availability eventual response.
limitations: Does not equate CAP consistency with ACID consistency.

title: Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store
claim: Concurrent versions require semantic reconciliation; union-style shopping-cart merging can resurrect deletions.
limitations: Historical Dynamo, not current DynamoDB; no implementation inspected.

title: Life beyond Distributed Transactions: an Apostate's Opinion
locator: §1 assumptions; pp.138-139 idempotence and remembered messages
claim: Explores entity-local serializability and durable message-processing state under a no-distributed-transactions assumption.
limitations: Explicit opinion; assumes a constraint rather than proving transactions impossible.

title: Spanner: Google's Globally-Distributed Database
claim: Combines replicated transaction state, two-phase commit and bounded-time uncertainty for externally consistent transactions.
limitations: No code or reproduction; does not remove partition tradeoffs.

title: How Do Committees Invent?
locator: A basic relationship; Systems Image Their Design Groups
claim: Explains relationship between organization communication and designed subsystem interfaces.
limitations: Conceptual argument, not deterministic predictive evidence.

title: Bounded Context
claim: Models can give shared words different meanings; integration needs explicit mappings.
limitations: Not Evans's original text; no automatic service-per-context implication.

title: Building Evolutionary Architectures — Engineering Incremental Change sample
locator: Engineering Incremental Change; pp.15-19 fitness categories/conflicting goals
claim: Describes targeted and system-wide checks for preserving architectural characteristics during incremental change.
limitations: Examples are not controlled comparisons; full book uninspected.

title: Monolith First
claim: Argues early service boundaries are uncertain and distribution adds costs; acknowledges sparse anecdotal evidence.
limitations: Not a universal rule or contemporary benchmark.

title: Don't start with a monolith
locator: subtitle; known domain; independent delivery; final caveats
claim: Argues early independently delivered subsystems can enforce separation when domain and need are understood.
context: Microservices as chosen goal; replacement systems.
limitations: Experience-based position; accepts small monoliths and boundary-change costs.

title: C4 Diagrams
claim: Different zoom levels address audiences; using every level is unnecessary.
limitations: Guidance, not measured sufficiency.

title: C4 Diagram FAQ
claim: Dependency and data-flow arrows need consistent labels; detail affects maintenance frequency.
limitations: Generation cannot prove unmodeled semantics or complete observation.

title: C4 Architecture Diagram Review Checklist
claim: Reviews scope, element type/purpose and relationship meaning/direction.
limitations: Passing notation checks is not correctness proof.

title: arc42 Runtime View
claim: Select representative significant runtime/error scenarios and map their actions to building blocks.
limitations: No obligation to diagram every scenario.

title: arc42 Quality Requirements
claim: Specific measurable usage/change scenarios make quality requirements assessable.
limitations: Scenario selection and thresholds remain project judgments.

title: Documenting Architecture Decisions
claim: Records significant decisions with forces, status and consequences; superseded decisions remain traceable.
limitations: Short early experience report, not universal efficacy evidence.

title: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter
claim: Retry amplification and ambiguous side effects require bounded ownership and idempotency.
limitations: Amazon experience; parameters are workload-specific.

title: Architecture of SQLite
claim: Explains SQL-to-bytecode execution and component/source ownership.
limitations: Descriptive documentation; not a comparative architecture study.

title: Atomic Commit in SQLite
claim: Explains rollback-journal crash recovery, assumptions and simulated-crash testing.
limitations: Historical passages coexist with updates; selected TRUNCATE prose differs from pinned code.

title: SQLite pager implementation
claim: Inspected journal/database sync ordering, finalization branches and conditional TRUNCATE sync.
limitations: Static inspection of conditional VFS sync request; no syscall/crash-test or latest-code claim.

title: PostgreSQL Architectural Fundamentals
claim: Documents client/server processes and per-connection backend model.
limitations: Simplified view omits many auxiliary processes.

title: PostgreSQL Transaction Isolation
claim: Distinguishes snapshot isolation from serializability; whole-transaction retry is part of the application contract.
limitations: No concurrency experiments performed.

title: PostgreSQL postmaster implementation
claim: Connection startup launches a backend; comments explain supervisor isolation from shared-memory and client blocking.
limitations: Narrow startup corroboration, not isolation-engine verification.

title: Kubernetes Controllers
locator: Controller pattern; API/direct control; desired/current state
claim: Explains control loops, desired state and separate controllers communicating through API state.
limitations: Live docs are newer than selected code; matched concepts only.

title: Kubernetes ReplicaSet controller implementation
claim: Checks expectations before Pod listing; gates mutation, maintains status, lowers failed-create expectations and rate-limits retries.
limitations: Not exactly-once proof; TODO notes missing create UID tracking.

title: Kubernetes ReplicaSet controller tests
claim: Tests encode create-failure limits, dormancy, expectation/listing order and slow-start batching.
limitations: Read only; no tests run; no live API-server timing evidence.

title: Kubernetes controller expectations utilities
claim: Expectations permit progress when fulfilled or expired; expiry is five minutes in selected revision.
limitations: Expiry is evaluated on checks and schedules no timer; in-memory expectations are not durable deduplication.

title: rust-analyzer architecture at pinned revision
locator: Bird's Eye View; crates/syntax L91+; hir L181+; invariants
claim: Documents deliberately absent dependencies and distinguishes internal representations from API boundaries.
context: IDE architecture and incomplete source input.
limitations: Documented intent; most invariants not checked against implementation.

title: rust-analyzer syntax dependency manifest
claim: Direct dependencies omit Salsa and LSP, consistent with the narrow documented syntax boundary.
context: Same revision as inspected architecture doc.
limitations: Does not prove absence of indirect coupling or runtime I/O.

title: Domain-Driven Design Reference
claim: No substantive claim extracted from inaccessible original.
limitations: Search snippets not treated as reading; Fowler interpretation used explicitly.
